claims.statement: The six shared framework targets have explicit inward build dependencies: Application depends on Domain; Persistence and Presentation on Application and Domain; Infrastructure on Persistence, Application and Domain; Remote Infrastructure on Infrastructure, Application and Domain. Both native app targets depend on all six.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests check app-target imports and selected implementation and platform imports across shared frameworks: five non-Presentation frameworks share a no-app-import list, Presentation has its own storage and platform import list, and Domain and Application receive additional restrictions; these exact-import guards are not a universal prohibition on conditional platform UI in Presentation.

Native apps assemble concrete stores and services; desktop WindowModel owns each window's workspace collection and navigation, while on mobile the shared MobileAppModel retains per-persistent-UIKit-session MobileWorkspaceSessionModel instances that own their own live workspaces and descriptors; MobileSceneModel selects within its bound session.

The MCP bridge is a separate authenticated stdio-to-HTTP executable, the widget renders ActivityKit workspace summaries, and the forwarding benchmark is a standalone shared-framework consumer rather than app/test-host logic. Frameworks/Resources is a synchronized input of TFM, TFI, FrameworkTests and TermindWidgets; WorkspaceActivitySupport is a synchronized input of TFI, TFITests and TermindWidgets, not a framework product. TFM's Embed MCP Bridge copy phase embeds termind-mcp, while TFI's Embed Foundation Extensions copy phase embeds TermindWidgets.appex.

AgentKit is a versioned remote Xcode package, not a declared maintenance submodule; Termind registers host-specific SSH/SFTP tools on its side of the host-neutral runtime boundary. The only submodule declared in .gitmodules is com.akinokaede.termind.

Cross-feature responsibility is split among Application policy, concrete shared adapters, Persistence stores and native owners: remote files use a filesystem port plus a transfer coordinator; Assistant execution uses an injected tool-registry factory; Vault sync uses persistence journals; speech uses an injected native audio input.

The reusable device directory follows shared-module ownership: Domain owns DeviceRecord, Application owns the repository port and observable model, and Persistence owns the SwiftData implementation. Native composition supplies the installation ID from VaultSyncJournal and platform-specific display-name acquisition: desktop MacDeviceName prefers trimmed nonempty kern.hostname with Device.current.safeDescription fallback, while mobile supplies Device.current.safeDescription directly; MacDeviceNameTests covers priority and nil, empty, and whitespace fallback.

TermindIOSApp is the mobile @main entrypoint, selecting live or test dependencies and constructing a MobileAppModel; MobileStartupView installs its container or displays unavailable content on initialization failure. Desktop TermindApp composes shared services for each WindowGroup, exits via the database-in-use guard when the store is occupied, and fatally terminates launch for other initialization errors.

MobileAppModel assembles persistence, connections, sync and Agent services, retains per-UIKit-session workspaces and exposes a flattened view; test or injected-host composition omits live sync and defaults Live Activities off. Presentation owns HostIconCatalog with empty-load fallback and override priority; distribution matching tries ID, then likeIDs, then generic Linux.

The Xcode target membership compiles WorkspaceActivitySupport source into TFI, TermindWidgets and TFITests; TFI embeds the widget extension, which directly depends on TermindPresentation, while TFM embeds the separate MCP bridge tool.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests enforce source-level ownership independently of target edges, protect benchmark independence, and keep resumable engines and multiplexer dialects behind Remote Infrastructure registries. RemoteConnectionCoordinator constructs clients and disconnects failed one-shot connections; mobile live assembly shares it across services, while testing defaults workspace connections to live despite in-memory storage. Its immutable engine registry selects Mosh and Eternal Terminal behind shared client lifecycle, rejects missing registration before side effects, and is tested for restore/retry without startup replay. A separate backend registry wraps multiplexer dialects. Remote Infrastructure directly links CSSH2, OpenSSL, TailscaleKit, MoshBootstrap, MoshCore, ETBootstrap and ETSession.
FrameworkTests directly depends on all six shared frameworks; the platform test targets depend on their app and selected shared frameworks rather than the standalone port-forwarding benchmark.

Shared Presentation has conditional AppKit and UIKit imports for rendering despite the architecture test's exact-line import exclusions; the import guard matches only unindented `import Module` lines, so it does not prove that all shared presentation views are platform-independent.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests enforce selected import and construction restrictions on native Application, UI and Features directories rather than a universal ban on native feature imports of shared frameworks; the AgentKit shadow-declaration guard scans the desktop source tree for an explicit set of runtime type names, not every AgentKit-related type across all targets.

Device directory changes use a device-kind History journal and native DeviceItem fields, separate from Vault records and journal. Both native apps gate device sync startup on Pro access, and the coordinator follows the master iCloud selection.

The device directory model registers the current installation on creation, caches ID-to-name lookups and tracks storage errors; the SwiftData implementation does not resurrect a remotely deleted device on launch registration, though explicit upsert can recreate it.

Device and connection-history synchronization use separate kind-filtered engines and states in the same CloudKit zone; after remote device changes, native composition reloads the device-directory model's cache.

Mobile Assistant assembly passes AgentHostServices.live the connection coordinator and SFTP concurrency scheduler, and injects native iOS audio input into shared speech transcription with interruption cancellation.

Mobile workspace activity links route to the persistent UIKit session that owns the workspace rather than moving its connection to the receiving window; independent-session and recovery behavior is covered by model tests, while native-window integration tests are opt-in with TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS=1 and serialized execution.

TermindAgentTools composes host-aware tools from injected host, connection, metrics, authentication, background, and optional scratch/pane services. General SSH run/stdin and mutating SFTP tools are acting-only, with separate planning SSH run/stdin registrations; absent optional capabilities omit their tools. Its presenter registry combines AgentKit built-in and Termind presenters; descriptor lookup rejects MCP targets and missing presenter IDs without a legacy-name fallback.

Xcode declares AgentKit as a remote upToNextMinorVersion package from 4.0.0 and resolution pins version 4.0.0 at 3481866cd47e83f6bf56b80c432c7824f61130b9; it is not a local package path or repository maintenance submodule.

Neither libssh2 nor Ghostty has a declared maintenance submodule. Xcode consumes libssh2-spm remotely with upToNextMinorVersion from 2.0.3-termind-4, resolved at 7ca39b8bcaf408351e8b6e4f449d2a39959bab49, and Lakr233/libghostty-spm from 2.2.2026101502, resolved to that version at 42bacd1339f323a693ddbca779295f4f77e5a697.

libtailscale-spm has no declared maintenance submodule; Xcode consumes its remote package through upToNextMinorVersion from 1.0.3, resolved to 1.0.3 at b58ed45fb22e53b472ccf6febde1f4a3ab08e295. TailscaleKit is a direct package product of Remote Infrastructure, not a shared framework target.

Remote Infrastructure owns the embedded userspace Tailscale node implementation; ArchitectureBoundaryTests rejects TailscaleKit and CTailscale imports in Domain, Application, Presentation, and Persistence.

Application owns TerminalFindController state and policy, with terminal actions and focus injected by native session/workspace owners. Dismissal retains query and optionally suppresses focus restoration; resize suspension prevents search/navigation until resume, which only restarts a still-presented nonempty query.

The reusable mobileToolbarSearch UIKit bridge owns native search attachment/responder transitions, defers synchronization from SwiftUI updates, fences presentation and edits during dismissal and restores the navigation owner's presentation context when removing its owned controller.
MobileWorkspaceSearchModifier owns feature-level search bindings: SSH, Mosh, Eternal Terminal and Telnet bind shared Find and dismiss without restoring terminal focus; SFTP binds the browser query.

FrameworkTests verifies terminal Find query retention, navigation without a query, and idempotent dismissal without terminal focus restoration; MobileShortcutTests verifies native Find key routing and that Escape remains terminal input unless Find is presented.
RemoteSessionBackendRegistry.live delegates backend construction to registered multiplexer dialects; tmux supplies RemoteTmuxBackend while socket dialects supply RemoteMultiplexerBackend.

Both native dependency assemblies layer SSHExecToolPresentation onto TermindAgentTools.presenterRegistry and resolve native presenters through the shared descriptor lookup, separating native SSH card presentation from host-tool registration.

Application's RemoteFileSystem is a Sendable async throwing file-operation port distinct from concrete SFTP clients and transfer coordination; its helpers sort directories first, validate file names, and mask permissions to 0o7777.

Application owns the RemoteSessionBackend contract and its injected factory registry; unregistered backend lookup throws RemoteSessionFailure.unsupported, and sessionExists propagates listing failures rather than interpreting them as proof that a session ended. Remote Infrastructure supplies the live dialect-backed factories.
